title: Runtime kernel handoff smoother and thermal-aware fallback policy
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Reduce oscillatory kernel switching and avoid tail-latency spikes when model execution path should transition between low-latency and high-throughput kernels. We will implement a lightweight online decision smoother that ingests short-window signals (seqlen histogram, KV cache hit ratio, GPU occupancy estimate, sustained SM throughput and device thermal headroom) and produces a stabilized kernel-selection decision with configurable hysteresis and failover actions.

Scope and motivation:
- Problem: rapid changes in incoming request characteristics (burst of long prefill requests, followed by decode-heavy short steps) combine with device-level perturbations (thermal throttling, transient memory pressure) to produce frequent kernel flips that increase overall tail latency and reduce effective throughput. Existing autotuners explore and then flip; we need operational smoothing and thermal fallbacks to keep SLAs.
- We are NOT replacing the kernel-cost model; instead we add an execution-time controller that (a) smooths noisy signals before committing a kernel swap, (b) enforces minimum dwell times and soft rollbacks, and (c) can trigger a safe fallback kernel when device telemetry indicates reduced headroom.

Design summary:
1) Inputs (1s sliding windows): local seqlen histogram (buckets), prefill ratio, KV cache hit rate, per-GPU sm_occupancy proxy, mem_bandwidth_saturation proxy, device_temp_delta (recent rise), and recent kernel switch count.
2) Signal normalizers: convert inputs to unitless scores in [0,1] using running percentiles and short EWMA baselines.
3) Decision function: weighted linear score combining latency-favoring and throughput-favoring components plus a thermal penalty. Tunable weights live in config (canary).
4) Smoothing layer: two-stage filter: (a) EWMA on the decision score with tau configurable per deployment tier, (b) minimum dwell time (configurable, default 1s) plus a hysteresis buffer to prevent flip-flops (require score delta > 0.15 to change kernel).
5) Thermal fallback: if device_temp_delta exceeds threshold OR mem_bandwidth_saturation > 0.9 for >500ms, immediately route new requests to a conservative fallback kernel implementation (lower occupancy but more robust memory usage) and flag for operator alert.
6) Prefetch probe: on suspected workload shifts (prefill ratio rise), schedule a micro-probe (one long-prefill request mirrored to probe path) to validate decision without impacting primary path. Probe results feed the EWMA.

Acceptance criteria (measurable):
- Canary perf: reduce kernel switches by >= 70% compared to baseline over a 24h mixed workload trace.
- Tail latency: p99 latency for decode requests under mixed load improves by >= 15% or stays within 5% of baseline if throughput improves.
- Safety: fallback path triggers must have <0.1% false positives in steady-state traffic.
- No user-facing errors introduced; any fallback must preserve correctness of outputs.

Instrumentation and dashboards:
- Add metrics: decision_score, smoothed_decision_score, current_kernel, kernel_switch_count, device_temp_delta, mem_bandwidth_saturation, probe_success_rate.
- Dashboard: runtime/kernel-handoff/v1 Canary dashboard (placeholder: https://perf.redwood.internal/dashboards/kernel-handoff-canary).

Rollout plan:
1) Unit tests + microbench harness that replays production request traces (tooling in infra/kernel-probe-harness).
2) Internal canary on staging pool with synthetic mixed workload for 48h.
3) Gradual canary in hosted (5% -> 20% -> 100%) with per-minute health checks and automated rollback on regression.
4) Add to Dedicated safe-mode toggle for customer operators.

Tasks (owner):
- Design doc: finalize scoring function and default weights (Aisha). Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.internal/pages/kernel-handoff-smoother (draft).
- Microbench harness: implement replay + probe injection (Liam). GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/XXXX
- Implement controller + metrics + config flags (Liam).
- E2E test: create mixed workload trace and canary script (SRE).
- Oncall playbook: list rollback triggers and incident runbook (Ops).

Trade-offs and risks:
- Smoothing increases inertia; if too aggressive it could delay beneficial kernel swaps and cost throughput. We'll expose tau and hysteresis thresholds to tune per deployment tier.
- Additional metrics add cardinality; we'll sample device telemetry at 250ms and only if running in canary mode.
- Probe mirroring incurs small extra cost; probes are rate-limited and capped (default 0.5% of requests).

Open questions:
- Optimal default dwell time per GPU class (A100 vs H100) — need microbench.
- Whether to integrate thermal-aware weight auto-tuning into Redwood Optimize later.

Notes: This ticket intentionally focuses on runtime control and safety hysteresis rather than long-running offline autotune experiments. It should integrate with existing kernel-cost-model outputs and warm-start policy from the autotuner (no duplication).
